svg.title: Crimping an Anderson Powerpole, step by step
svg.desc: Animated, six steps in a 12 second loop, with a numbered step list that lights up in step. 1: strip 5/16 in (7.9 mm); the cut piece of red insulation slides off the bare strands. FRC motor leads are usually 12 AWG; contacts are 30 A for 16-12 AWG and 45 A for 14-10 AWG. 2: the contact sits open in a Powerpole crimp tool and the wire slides in until the copper reaches the wire stop, not past it, with the insulation just short of the barrel. 3: the jaws close and the barrel grips bare copper only. 4: check the crimp: bare copper only in the barrel, the tab not spread and no solder; nothing past the wire stop; the insulation just short of the barrel, leaving a small bare gap. 5: push the contact into the housing, its hooked edge toward the flat spring, until it clicks: the spring is pressed down as the hook passes, then snaps up behind it. 6: tug the wire, then push the contact from the front: a seated contact holds 20 lb. A still panel shows the mating face: black (-) on the left, red (+) on the right, tongues on top - red right, tongue top - so every pair built that way mates with every other; slide the dovetails together, never snap them on sideways. With reduced motion the drawing shows the checked crimp.
svg.text: Crimping an Anderson Powerpole, step by step
